name: The Light Table
tagline: The homepage as a contact sheet on a light table: the photographs carry all the colour, the interface recedes to quiet gallery labels.
thesis: Image-first to the point of disappearance: sharp square prints (a 6x6 medium-format contact sheet that uses the 480px thumbs natively), captions set like museum wall labels (title, minutes, lei), and a neutral paper/graphite system whose only colour is a china-marker red that underlines what you chose. A daily-rotating 'today's plate' answers the greeting 'Ce gătim azi?' with a real recipe that develops like a print on load, so the page feels curated without inventing any content.
fonts: Archivo (expanded width 112–125%, light 300) — wall titles: greeting, category rooms, brand wordmark
Archivo (normal width, 480–650, tabular figures) — labels, controls, minutes and lei

palette.name: China marker
palette.role: Active sort underline and filter badge (dark: #F0675B)

highlights: First mobile viewport (390x844): greeting, today's plate with title/min/lei, the full control strip and the first row of prints with titles.

Control strip is one sticky row down to 360px (count, category switch, Name/Time/Price with arrow + hand-drawn underline); results are filtered via the drawer and shown as removable tags on the page; the opening collapses while searching/filtering so results come first.
Price is typographic, not an emoji: '≈ 2,04 lei' marks partial estimates (title + screen-reader label), '— lei' for unavailable; locale-aware decimals.

Drawer with image-led category index (thumb + name + live count, empty ones disabled), AND chips, More links and RO/EN, light/dark, normal/large segmented radios; inert background, Escape/backdrop close, scroll lock, focus return.
Sort/group/filter changes reorder prints with the View Transitions API (FLIP for free); reduced-motion disables all of it and the print 'develop' moment.
tradeoffs: Single typeface on purpose (width axis as hierarchy); needs a variable Archivo build with the wdth axis in production.
The featured plate changes daily (seeded by date), so screenshots and first impressions vary; square crops of 3:2 photos may clip some plated dishes.
View Transitions is Chromium/Safari-only; other browsers get instant (still correct) re-renders.
